recipes.name: Elote
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, chewy corn on the cob under a creamy, salty coat of crema, mayonnaise and cotija, sharpened with chile and lime.
recipes.healthBenefit: Whole corn brings fibre and some B vitamins, while the mayonnaise, crema and cheese make each ear a rich street treat.

ingredients.prepNote: Mexican elote is large, starchy white corn; boil in the husk or grill

instructions: Pull the outer husks back but leave the inner ones on, and trim the ends.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add the corn, cover and cook over medium heat for 8 to 12 minutes, until the kernels are tender. To grill instead, cook over medium coals for 10 to 15 minutes, turning every few minutes until charred in spots.
Pull off the husks and silk, then push a wooden stick into the base of each ear if you like.
Brush each hot ear with crema, then a thin layer of mayonnaise.
Roll or sprinkle with crumbled cotija, dust with chile piquín, and squeeze lime over just before eating.

citations.source: Mexico in My Kitchen, Mexican Corn on the Cob (Elote)
Camila Made, Elote

recipes.curationNote: Both sources dress the boiled or grilled ear with crema, mayonnaise, cotija, ground chile and lime; Mexico in My Kitchen boils it in the husk as in Mexico, so that is the main method.

recipes.name: Esquites
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender corn kernels in a little epazote broth, piled into a cup with mayonnaise, lime, cheese and a sting of chile.
recipes.healthBenefit: Corn kernels give fibre and potassium, and the epazote broth keeps it lighter than elote, though the toppings still add fat.
instructions: Heat the butter and oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Fry the árbol chiles for 20 to 30 seconds until they darken a shade, then lift them out and crumble them.
Add the onion and cook 3 to 4 minutes until soft, then add the corn kernels and stir for 4 to 5 minutes.
Pour in the water, add the epazote, salt and the crumbled chile, bring to a simmer and cook covered for 15 to 25 minutes, until the kernels are tender and the broth is flavourful.
Spoon the corn with some of its broth into cups. Top each with mayonnaise, a squeeze of lime, queso fresco and cotija, and a pinch of chile piquín.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the corn and its cooking broth.

citations.source: Pati Jinich, Esquites con Pepitas y Chile de Árbol
Rick Bayless, Esquites

recipes.curationNote: Pati Jinich fries árbol chile in butter and oil then simmers the kernels with epazote in water; Bayless simmers 20 to 30 minutes with epazote. The pepitas in Pati version are left off as the plain street version.

recipes.name: Gorditas de Chicharrón Prensado
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, puffed masa cakes, crisp outside and soft inside, filled with rich, chile-stewed pressed pork crackling and topped with salsa, onion and cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: The masa gives calcium from the nixtamal and some fibre, while the pressed pork and the fat they fry in make these a hearty, rich antojito.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, corn flour, masa, yellow, U.S. enriched
Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

ingredients.name: chicharrón prensado (pressed pork cracklings in chile)

instructions: Mix the masa harina, wheat flour, salt and baking powder, then work in the warm water a little at a time until the dough is soft and does not crack, about 3 to 5 minutes. Cover and rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. Flatten each one, put a spoonful of chopped chicharrón in the centre, close the dough over it and press it into a disc about 1 cm thick.
Cook each gordita on a hot comal over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes a side to set the surface.
Heat the lard in a skillet to about 350°F (175°C) and fry the gorditas 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and puffed. Drain on paper.
Slit one side if you like and serve topped with salsa verde, onion, cilantro and crumbled queso fresco.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the nixtamalized masa and the cheese.
From the pressed pork and cheese.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta de gorditas de chicharrón
Grupo Animal, Gorditas de chicharrón prensado

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior gives quantities (masa harina with a little wheat flour and baking powder, 150 g chicharrón, fried in lard 1 cm thick); Grupo Animal confirms filling, frying and toppings.

recipes.name: Molletes con Pico de Gallo
recipes.flavorProfile: Toasty halved bolillos spread with warm refried beans under bubbling melted cheese, cooled with fresh pico de gallo.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beans bring fibre, protein and folate to a simple breakfast, with cheese adding calcium.

ingredients.prepNote: Mexican manchego is a mild melting cheese; Chihuahua works too

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Split the bolillos lengthwise and pull out a little of the soft crumb. Spread the cut sides thinly with butter.
Spread each half with warm refried beans and cover with the cheese.
Bake on a tray for 10 to 14 minutes, until the bread is crisp at the edges and the cheese has melted.
Serve hot with pico de gallo spooned on top.

citations.source: México Desconocido, Molletes
Adán Medrano, Molletes

recipes.curationNote: Both sources: bolillo halves, refritos, cheese, baked, with pico de gallo. Manchego per México Desconocido; 350°F and about 12 minutes per Medrano.

recipes.name: Molotes de Papa con Chorizo
recipes.flavorProfile: Long, crisp fried masa pockets with a soft centre of potato and spicy chorizo, served with crema, cheese and salsa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potato and masa give energy and some potassium, while chorizo and deep frying make molotes a rich evening treat.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, corn flour, masa, yellow, U.S. enriched
Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

instructions: Cook the onion in a little of the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes, add the chorizo and break it up, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until done. Stir in the boiled potato and season with salt.
Mix the masa harina, wheat flour, baking powder, lard and a pinch of salt, then knead in the warm water until smooth and moist, 3 to 5 minutes.
Roll small balls of dough between two sheets of plastic into ovals about 12 by 6 cm. Spoon filling down the centre, fold over into a half moon and press the edges well so nothing leaks.
Heat the oil to about 350°F (175°C) and fry the molotes 4 to 6 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper.
Serve on shredded lettuce with crema, queso fresco and salsa.

citations.source: Kiwilimón, Molotes Poblanos
Larousse Cocina, Molote (Diccionario enciclopédico de la gastronomía mexicana)

recipes.curationNote: Kiwilimón gives the Puebla dough with wheat flour and baking powder and the potato with chorizo filling; Larousse confirms the Puebla shape (12 by 6 cm half moon) and papa con longaniza or chorizo as a classic filling.

recipes.name: Quesadillas de Flor de Calabaza
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft fresh masa folded around stretchy Oaxaca cheese and tender squash blossoms with epazote, toasted on the comal until spotted.
recipes.healthBenefit: Squash blossoms are light and bring vitamin A precursors, and the nixtamal masa gives calcium, with the cheese adding protein.

ingredients.cutPrep: stems and pistils removed, roughly chopped

instructions: Cook the onion and serrano in the oil over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, add the squash blossoms and epazote, season with salt and cook 3 to 5 minutes until wilted and the liquid is gone.
Divide the masa into 10 balls and press each between plastic in a tortilla press into a round about 12 cm across.
Lay a raw tortilla on a hot comal over medium heat. Put cheese and blossoms on one half and fold it over, pressing the edges.
Cook about 3 minutes a side, turning once or twice, until the masa is cooked through with brown spots and the cheese has melted.
Serve hot with salsa.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the nixtamal masa and the cheese.

citations.source: México Desconocido, Quesadillas de flor de calabaza
Maricruz Avalos, Quesadillas de Flor de Calabaza

recipes.curationNote: The Mexico City quesadilla made from raw fresh masa on the comal, as in México Desconocido (1 kg masa for 10 people, 12 cm tortillas, 3 minutes a side); Maricruz Avalos gives the onion, chile and epazote sauté. Halved for 5.

recipes.name: Sincronizadas
recipes.flavorProfile: Two flour tortillas pressed around ham and melted cheese, toasted crisp and cut in wedges, with guacamole and salsa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ham and cheese make this a protein-rich quick meal, though it is salty, and the guacamole adds fibre and good fats.
instructions: Heat a comal or skillet over medium heat and wipe it with a little oil.
Lay one tortilla down, cover with half its share of cheese, two slices of ham and the rest of the cheese, then top with a second tortilla.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes, pressing with a spatula, until the underside is golden in spots and the cheese starts to melt.
Flip and cook another 2 to 3 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese has melted. Repeat with the rest.
Cut into wedges and serve warm with guacamole and pico de gallo.

citations.source: Pati Jinich, Ham and Cheese Quesadillas (Sincronizadas)
Mexico in My Kitchen, Quesadillas or Sincronizadas

recipes.curationNote: Both use flour tortillas with ham and Chihuahua or Oaxaca cheese, cooked on the comal and served with guacamole and salsa. Pati: 12 tortillas, 8 oz cheese, 6 to 12 ham slices.

recipes.name: Sopes
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick little masa boats with pinched rims, crisp on the bottom, layered with beans, shredded chicken, lettuce, crema and crumbly cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beans and chicken give protein and fibre on a calcium-bearing nixtamal base, with fresh lettuce on top.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, corn flour, masa, yellow, U.S. enriched

instructions: Mix the masa harina, salt and warm water into a soft dough that does not stick, 2 to 3 minutes. Divide into 10 balls and keep them covered.
Press each ball into a thick round about 1 cm thick and 8 cm across. Cook on a hot comal over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until the surface sets.
While they are still hot, pinch up a rim all around each one with your fingertips, protecting your hands with a towel.
Melt the lard in a skillet over medium heat and fry the sopes, rim side up, 1 to 2 minutes, spooning a little fat inside, until crisp underneath.
Spread with beans and top with chicken, lettuce, onion, crema, crumbled queso fresco and salsa.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the nixtamal masa and cheese.

citations.source: Mexico in My Kitchen, Sopes
La Cocina de Leslie, How to Make Mexican Sopes

recipes.curationNote: Mexico in My Kitchen: 10 sopes from 1.5 cups masa harina, fried in lard or oil, beans, shredded meat, lettuce, queso fresco, crema; rims pinched while hot. La Cocina de Leslie confirms the method.

recipes.name: Tlacoyos
recipes.region: Mexico City and the State of Mexico
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, pointed masa ovals with a seam of creamy bean inside, toasted on the comal and topped with tangy nopales, salsa, onion and cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: Masa and beans together give fibre and plant protein, and a nopal topping adds more fibre for very little fat.

components.note: about 180 g, thick and well fried

ingredients.cutPrep: cleaned, diced and boiled until tender

instructions: Knead the masa with the salt, adding a spoon of water if it cracks, until soft and smooth. Divide into 6 balls and keep them covered.
Press each ball between plastic into a thick round about 12 cm across. Spoon about 1½ tablespoons of beans down the middle, fold the round over to seal, and pinch each end into a point.
Pat the filled tlacoyo flat again to about 2 cm thick, keeping the oval shape.
Cook on a comal over medium heat greased with a little lard, 2 to 4 minutes a side, turning a few times, until speckled and cooked through.
Top with the boiled nopales, salsa, crumbled cheese, onion and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beans, masa and nopales.
From the nixtamal masa and the cheese.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Tlacoyos (Alicia Gironella)
Mexico in My Kitchen, How to Make Tlacoyos

recipes.curationNote: Larousse (Alicia Gironella): fresh masa, beans or requesón, 2 cm thick ovals cooked on a greased comal, topped with nopales or quelites, cheese, onion and salsa. Mexico in My Kitchen gives the quantities for 6 and the pointed shape.

recipes.name: Tlayuda
recipes.flavorProfile: A huge, crackling-crisp Oaxacan tortilla smeared with pork asiento and black beans, folded over strings of quesillo, cabbage and grilled tasajo.
recipes.healthBenefit: Black beans and beef make it filling and protein-rich, and cabbage adds crunch and vitamin C, though the asiento and cheese make it rich.

components.note: about 800 g fresh masa for 4 large tlayudas
black beans, about 350 g, ideally cooked with hoja santa
chile de árbol salsa, for serving

ingredients.name: asiento (the browned pork fat from the bottom of the chicharrón pot)
ingredients.prepNote: or unto; lard can stand in

instructions: Press the masa into 4 very thin rounds about 30 cm across, using two sheets of plastic. Cook each on a large comal over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side, then leave it on the edge of the comal to dry and toast until stiff, 10 to 15 minutes. This is the tlayuda.
Grill the tasajo over hot coals or in a hot skillet for 2 to 3 minutes a side and cut it into pieces.
Warm a tlayuda on the comal for a few seconds to soften it a little. Spread it thinly with asiento, then with a layer of the black beans blended with hoja santa.
Scatter cabbage and quesillo over one half, fold the other half over, and toast it over medium heat or on a grill over coals, 5 to 10 minutes a side, until crisp and the cheese melts.
Serve with the tasajo on top or alongside, avocado, and the chile de árbol salsa.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tasajo, beans and quesillo.
From the black beans and masa.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Tlayuda istmeña
Animal Gourmet, Cómo hacer tlayudas oaxaqueñas

recipes.curationNote: Animal Gourmet gives the Central Valleys version: asiento, black beans blended with hoja santa, tasajo, cabbage and quesillo. Larousse gives the fold-and-toast method with unto, 10 minutes a side. The tortilla itself is made here from the masa base, since no tlayuda shell base exists.

recipes.name: Tostadas de Tinga de Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy tostadas spread with beans and piled with smoky chipotle chicken and onion, cooled with lettuce, avocado, crema and crumbled cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and beans make this a protein-rich plate with fibre, and the fresh toppings add vitamins, with crema and cheese in moderation.

ingredients.name: chipotle chiles in adobo
ingredients.cutPrep: chopped, with a spoon of their sauce

instructions: Simmer the tomatoes and garlic in salted water for 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Peel the tomatoes and blend them with the garlic and the chipotles until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the sliced onion for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and translucent.
Pour in the tomato and chipotle sauce, add the bay leaves and salt, and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in the shredded chicken and cook 5 to 10 minutes more, until most of the sauce clings to the meat.
Spread each tostada with refried beans and top with tinga, lettuce, avocado, crema and queso fresco. Serve the salsa on the side.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beans, avocado and lettuce.

citations.source: Pati Jinich, Chicken Tinga Tostadas
Larousse Cocina, Tostadas de tinga de pollo y de pata (Aquiles Chávez)

recipes.curationNote: Tinga is the classic Puebla tostada topping. Larousse gives the tinga (boiled tomato and garlic, sliced onion, bay, chipotle); Pati gives the assembly for 12 tostadas with beans, lettuce, avocado, queso fresco and crema.

recipes.name: Corundas
recipes.flavorProfile: Small, five-sided Purépecha tamales with a light, slightly salty masa, served under a mild tomato and poblano sauce with sour cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: Plain corn masa gives energy and calcium from the nixtamal, while the lard makes these rich, so the vegetable sauce is a good partner.

components.note: about 1 kg fresh masa, coarsely ground if you can get it

ingredients.name: fresh green corn plant leaves (hojas de milpa)
poblano chiles
ingredients.cutPrep: roasted, peeled, seeded and cut in strips

instructions: For the sauce, cook the onion in the teaspoon of lard over medium heat for 3 minutes, add the garlic and poblano strips and cook 3 minutes more.
Blend the roasted tomatoes, add them to the pan and boil 5 minutes until reduced by half. Add the chicken stock, cook 5 minutes more, salt to taste and set aside.

For the masa, mix the masa with the water. Beat the 350 g of lard for 5 minutes until white and fluffy, then beat in the masa a little at a time with the baking powder and salt, 5 minutes more. It should taste lightly salty.
Fold a milpa leaf from its thick end into a cone, put in about 2 tablespoons of masa, and keep folding the leaf up and around to make a five-sided tamal. Repeat with the rest.
Steam over high heat for about 1 hour, until the masa comes away cleanly from the leaf, then rest 20 minutes. Unwrap and serve with the sauce and crema.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomato and poblano sauce.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Corundas (Margarita Carrillo)
Animal Gourmet, Qué son y cómo se preparan las corundas michoacanas

recipes.curationNote: Followed Margarita Carrillo Arronte (Larousse): 15 corundas from 1 kg masa and 350 g lard, wrapped in milpa leaves, tomato and poblano rajas sauce with crema. Animal Gourmet (Alicia Gironella) confirms the leaf folding and the 1 hour steam; its rice flour and cheese variant was not used.

recipes.name: Uchepos
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet fresh corn tamales with a custardy crumb, eaten warm with cream, crumbled cheese and a little red salsa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made from fresh corn kernels, uchepos bring fibre and some vitamin C, while the cream and sugar make them a rich treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: kernels from about 10 to 12 tender ears

ingredients.prepNote: stands in for nata, the skin skimmed from boiled milk

instructions: Carefully peel the husks from the ears and keep the inner ones in a bowl of water. Cut the kernels from the cobs.
Blend the kernels with a little of the cream until as smooth as you can get them, without adding water.
Beat the rest of the cream with the sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir it into the corn purée.

Lay a fresh husk (or two thin ones) with its point toward you, spread about 3 tablespoons of the mixture in the middle, fold the sides in and the point up, and stand the uchepos open end up in a steamer lined with husks.
Cover with more husks and steam over high heat for about 1 hour, until they come away easily from the husk. Serve warm with cream, cheese and red salsa.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Uchepos (Ricardo Muñoz Zurita)
Pati Jinich, Uchepos, tamales de elote

recipes.curationNote: Ricardo Muñoz Zurita (Larousse): 12 tender ears, 3 cups nata, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, steamed 1 hour. Pati uses condensed milk and a little flour instead; the nata version was kept as the Michoacán one, with sugar trimmed to the lower end. Heavy cream stands in for nata. Michoacán serving with red salsa and cheese from the Larousse dictionary entry.

recipes.name: Tamales Rojos de Cerdo
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy, lard-beaten masa wrapped around tender shredded pork in a deep red guajillo and ancho sauce, steamed in corn husks.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork shoulder brings protein, zinc and B vitamins and the chiles add vitamin A precursors, while the lard-beaten masa makes these a rich festive food.

components.note: enough beaten masa for 16 tamales, about 1.3 kg

ingredients.cutPrep: a quarter onion in one piece

ingredients.name: dried corn husks
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in hot water 20 to 30 minutes until pliable

instructions: Put the pork, garlic, onion, bay leaf and salt in a pot, cover with the water, bring to a boil and simmer partly covered for about 1 hour, skimming, until tender enough to shred. Shred the meat and keep the broth for the masa.
Soak the ancho chiles in hot water for 15 to 20 minutes, then blend them into the guajillo salsa with the cumin.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium high heat, pour in the chile sauce with 240 ml of the pork broth and cook 8 minutes. Add the pork, season with salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes more until thick and flavourful.
Spread about ⅓ cup of the beaten masa on the wide end of a drained husk, put a spoonful of pork down the middle, fold the sides over and fold the narrow end up.

Stand the tamales open end up in a steamer lined with husks, cover with more husks and a lid, and steam over medium heat for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the masa comes away cleanly from the husk. Rest 15 minutes before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the ancho and guajillo chiles.

citations.source: Mexico in My Kitchen, Tamales Rojos de Puerco
Rick Bayless, Red Chile Pork Tamales Steamed in Corn Husks

recipes.curationNote: Mexico in My Kitchen gives the 16-tamal batch (3/4 lb pork, ancho and guajillo, 1 hour 15 minutes); Bayless describes the central Mexico style as light and fluffy with guajillo pork. The guajillo sauce base carries the guajillos; the ancho is added here.

recipes.name: Tamales de Elote
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, tender fresh corn tamales with butter and a hint of canela, soft and moist like a steamed corn cake.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh corn kernels give fibre and potassium, while the butter and sugar make these a sweet treat for the afternoon.

ingredients.name: sweetened condensed milk
ingredients.prepNote: optional, for a sweeter tamal; leave out and add 50 g more sugar if you prefer

instructions: Peel the husks from the ears carefully and keep them in water. Cut off the kernels.
Grind the kernels in a blender or food processor with the butter, sugar, condensed milk, canela, baking powder and salt until you have a thick, slightly coarse batter.
Spread a heaped tablespoon or two of the batter on each husk, fold it into a small packet and tie it with a strip of husk.
Line a steamer with husks, stand the tamales in it, cover with more husks and steam over medium heat for 40 to 60 minutes, until they come away easily from the husk.
Rest a few minutes and serve warm, plain or with a spoon of crema.

citations.source: Cocina Fácil, Tamal de elote dulce
Mexico in My Kitchen, Sweet Corn Tamales (Tamales de Elote)

recipes.curationNote: Cocina Fácil: kernels ground with butter, condensed milk, canela, baking powder and salt, steamed 30 to 40 minutes in fresh husks. Mexico in My Kitchen confirms butter, sugar, baking powder and salt in fresh husks. Its masa harina was left out to keep the all-corn street version; the separate Michoacán uchepo uses nata.

recipes.name: Tamales de Dulce
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy pink sweet tamales studded with raisins, lightly sweet and tender, the classic partner for atole or champurrado.
recipes.healthBenefit: These are a festive sweet: corn masa gives some calcium, but the sugar and lard make them a treat rather than an everyday food.

ingredients.name: red food colouring (or a little cochineal, as was done before)
dried corn husks
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in hot water 20 to 30 minutes until pliable

instructions: Beat the lard with the baking powder at high speed for 3 to 5 minutes until white and fluffy like meringue.
In a large bowl, beat the masa and water together by hand until no lumps are left. Add the sugar, raisins and colouring and mix again.
Fold in the beaten lard until the mixture is even.
Spread about ⅓ cup of masa on each drained husk, fold the sides over each other and fold the point up without squeezing.
Stand the tamales open end up in a steamer over water, bring to a full steam over high heat and cook for 1 hour. Turn off the heat and rest at least 20 minutes before serving.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Tamales de dulce (Ricardo Muñoz Zurita)
Mexico in My Kitchen, Sweet Tamales (Tamales Dulces)

recipes.curationNote: Followed Ricardo Muñoz Zurita (Larousse) for 18 tamales: 1 kg masa, about 1¼ cups lard, 1¼ cups sugar, ¼ cup raisins, red colouring once made with cochineal, 1 hour steam. Mexico in My Kitchen confirms the method with butter.

recipes.name: Tamales Oaxaqueños de Mole Negro
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, moist masa steamed flat in banana leaf around chicken and pork in dark, bittersweet mole negro, with the leaf giving a grassy perfume.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and pork give protein, and the chiles, seeds and chocolate in the mole bring minerals, while the lard masa makes these a festive, rich food.

components.note: about 1.2 kg beaten masa, loosened with extra broth to a very soft, spreadable texture

ingredients.name: banana leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: large leaves, softened and cut in 20 cm squares

instructions: Cover the pork with water, add the garlic and onion and simmer for 30 minutes. Add the chicken, salt and more boiling water and simmer 30 to 40 minutes more until both are tender. Lift out the meat, take the chicken off the bone and cut everything in medium pieces. Keep the broth.
Soften the banana leaves by passing them over a flame for a few seconds a side, or boiling them about 20 minutes until they lose their bright green. Cut into 20 cm squares and wipe them clean.
Dissolve the mole in a little of the fat skimmed from the broth and heat it until thick and glossy, 5 to 10 minutes.
Beat a little more warm broth into the tamal masa until very soft and spreadable.

Spread a thin layer of masa over the middle of a banana leaf square, add a spoon of mole and two spoons of meat, fold the leaf in three from the sides and then the ends to make a flat square, and tie with a strip of leaf.
Lay the tamales flat in layers in a steamer, cover and steam for about 1 hour 30 minutes, adding boiling water as needed. They are done when the masa comes away from the leaf.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dried chiles, seeds and chocolate in the mole.
From the seeds and cacao in the mole negro.

citations.source: ¡Hola! Cocina, Tamales oaxaqueños (Fundación Casa de México en España)
Los Sabores de México, Oaxacan Tamales

recipes.curationNote: Fundación Casa de México: pork and whole chicken, 500 g mole negro, 250 g lard beaten with masa and broth, banana leaf squares folded in three, steamed 1 hour 30 minutes. Los Sabores de México confirms grilling the leaves, tying with leaf strips and the same steaming time.

recipes.name: Huitlacoche Guisado
recipes.flavorProfile: Earthy, smoky-sweet corn mushroom sautéed with onion, garlic and epazote, ready to tuck into tortillas or quesadillas.
recipes.healthBenefit: Huitlacoche is low in fat and brings protein, fibre and some minerals, and the epazote and onion add flavour without much salt.

ingredients.name: huitlacoche (fresh or frozen)
ingredients.cutPrep: rinsed and cut in bite-size pieces

instructions: Heat the oil in a medium frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for about 2 minutes until it turns translucent, add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the huitlacoche and epazote. It will release some liquid as it cooks; stir lightly and keep sautéing for about 5 minutes, until just tender. Do not overcook it or it turns dry.
Season with salt and serve about 2 tablespoons in each warm tortilla, with a raw serrano salsa, or use it to fill quesadillas with melting cheese.

nutritionHighlights.note: Huitlacoche carries more protein than the corn it grows on.

citations.source: Mexico in My Kitchen, Huitlacoche Tacos
UTSA La Cocina Histórica, Huitlacoche con Rajas, Crema y Queso 1971 (from La Cocina de Doña Ventura)

recipes.curationNote: Mely Martínez: 1 lb huitlacoche, onion, garlic, epazote, about 5 minutes, served in tortillas with raw serrano salsa. The 1971 Doña Ventura recipe confirms frying chopped huitlacoche with onion in hot oil and serving it with hot tortillas. The rajas and cream variant was not used.

recipes.name: Nopales a la Mexicana
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender strips of nopal cooked with tomato, onion and serrano, bright and a little tangy, eaten with tortillas or beside eggs and beans.
recipes.healthBenefit: Nopales are very low in calories and rich in fibre, and the tomato adds vitamin C, so this is a light, filling vegetable dish.
instructions: Simmer the nopal strips in salted water for about 10 minutes, until they turn olive green and tender. Drain and rinse to remove the slime.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and serrano for 3 to 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and cook 3 to 5 minutes until it gives up its juice.
Stir in the nopales, lower the heat and cook a few minutes more. Season with salt and serve with hot tortillas or beside eggs and beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: Nopales are rich in soluble fibre.

citations.source: Excélsior, Recetas con nopales para Cuaresma (Nopales a la mexicana)
El Universal, 5 deliciosas maneras de preparar nopales

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior gives the dish for 4: 6 cooked nopales in strips, 1 cup tomato, ½ cup onion, 1 serrano, oil and salt. El Universal confirms cooking nopales no more than 10 minutes and pairing them with tomato, onion and cilantro. Salt cut from 1 tablespoon to 1 teaspoon in the dish, with the rest in the boiling water.

recipes.name: Rajas con Crema y Elote
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky strips of roasted poblano and sweet corn in a silky cream sauce, mild and comforting, perfect in tacos.
recipes.healthBenefit: Poblano chiles are rich in vitamin C and corn adds fibre, while the cream makes it rich, so it pairs well with tortillas and beans.

ingredients.name: poblano chiles
ingredients.cutPrep: about 500 g, charred, peeled, seeded and cut in 1 cm strips

instructions: Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under the grill until the skin is black and blistered all over, 6 to 10 minutes. Seal them in a bag for 10 minutes to sweat.
Rub off the skin under cold water, remove the seeds and white veins, and cut into strips about 1 cm wide.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan and cook the onion over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the corn and the poblano strips and cook 5 minutes over medium heat.
Turn the heat to low, stir in the crema, season with salt and pepper and warm through for 2 to 3 minutes without boiling. Serve with hot tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: Poblano chiles are a rich source.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta de rajas con crema: el secreto para que no piquen
Grupo Animal, Rajas con crema y elote

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior gives the quantities: 500 g poblano, 250 ml crema, 150 g corn, 100 g onion, 30 ml oil, optional panela. Grupo Animal adds blended cream cheese and manchego; left out here to keep the plain home version.

recipes.name: Calabacitas con Queso
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender Mexican squash with tomato, onion and a little serrano, finished with soft cubes of melting fresh cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: Squash and tomato are low in calories and bring vitamin C and potassium, and the cheese adds protein and calcium.

ingredients.cutPrep: Mexican grey squash or zucchini, cut in cubes

instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat, add the squash and cook for 2 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the serrano, onion, garlic, tomato, salt and pepper, stir and cook for about 5 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Stir in the cheese, turn off the heat, cover and leave 2 minutes so it softens. Serve as a side, or as a light meal with tortillas.

citations.source: Mama Maggie’s Kitchen, Calabacitas con Queso (Maggie Unzueta)
Maricruz Avalos, Calabacitas con Queso

recipes.curationNote: Followed Maggie Unzueta: calabacitas, serrano, onion, garlic, tomato and cubed panela, 7 minutes. Maricruz Avalos makes a fuller version with corn, poblano, cumin and Oaxaca cheese; those were not added. Her note on epazote or oregano is a fair option.

recipes.name: Tortitas de Camarón
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, puffy fritters of beaten egg and ground dried shrimp, salty and savoury, made to simmer in mole with romeritos.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs and dried shrimp make these protein-rich, and dried shrimp is salty, so no salt is added.

ingredients.name: dried shrimp
ingredients.cutPrep: heads, tails and shells removed, ground to a fine powder

instructions: Peel the dried shrimp and grind them to a fine powder in a blender or spice grinder.
Beat the egg whites until they hold stiff peaks, then beat in the yolks one at a time and fold in the shrimp powder to make a soft paste.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat to about 175°C (350°F). Drop in teaspoons of the paste and fry for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until puffed and golden, without letting them burn.
Drain on paper towels. Keep them apart from the mole until the moment of serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: Dried shrimp is a sea food source.

citations.source: Los Sabores de México, Romeritos con mole y tortitas de camarón
ADN40, Receta fácil para preparar romeritos (chef Denisse Palacios)

recipes.curationNote: Written as a base for the romeritos. Both sources beat the whites to stiff peaks, add the yolks and ground shrimp, and fry spoonfuls in hot oil. Halved from Los Sabores de México (1/4 kg shrimp, 6 eggs).

recipes.name: Romeritos en Mole con Tortitas de Camarón
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender, slightly salty romerito greens in rich red mole with little potatoes, nopales and puffy dried shrimp fritters, the classic Christmas Eve dish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Romeritos are a leafy green with vitamins and minerals, nopales add fibre and the shrimp fritters protein, while the mole is rich.

components.note: about 500 g mole, loosened with stock

ingredients.name: romeritos (seepweed greens)
ingredients.cutPrep: thick stems and roots removed, washed
a piece, for the nopal water

instructions: Wash the romeritos well to remove all soil. Boil them in salted water for 5 to 10 minutes, until tender enough to break with a fingernail, then cool under cold water and drain.
Boil the small potatoes in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until tender. Separately, boil the diced nopales with a piece of onion and salt for about 10 minutes, drain and rinse.
In a deep pot, dissolve the mole in the chicken stock and simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring, until it is smooth and coats a spoon lightly.
At the moment of serving, add the romeritos, potatoes, nopales and shrimp fritters to the mole and heat for 5 minutes. Store the parts separately and heat only what you will serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the romeritos, nopales and potatoes.
From the leafy greens and mole.

citations.source: Los Sabores de México, Romeritos con mole y tortitas de camarón
ADN40, Receta fácil para preparar romeritos (chef Denisse Palacios)

recipes.curationNote: Los Sabores de México: 1.5 kg romeritos, potatoes, optional nopales, mole paste with chicken broth simmered 30 minutes, everything added only at serving. ADN40 (Denisse Palacios) adds the boiling times and the fingernail test. Halved to about 1 kg greens.

recipes.name: Camotes Enmielados
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole sweet potatoes slowly simmered in dark piloncillo syrup with canela, clove and anise until soft and glossy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sweet potato is rich in beta carotene and fibre, but the syrup is sugary, so this is a sweet side for special days.

components.note: about 225 g piloncillo dissolved in 480 ml water, with the cinnamon stick

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 large sweet potatoes, scrubbed, whole or in large pieces

instructions: Put the sweet potatoes in a heavy pot with the piloncillo syrup, anise, clove and orange slices. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for about 50 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are soft.
Uncover and simmer gently 15 to 20 minutes more so the syrup reduces to a thick honey.
Rest 10 minutes, remove the spices and orange, and serve each sweet potato with syrup spooned over, warm or cold.

nutritionHighlights.note: Sweet potato is rich in beta carotene.

citations.source: Isabel Eats, Camote Enmielado
Grupo Animal, Cómo preparar dulce de camote casero

recipes.curationNote: Isabel Eats: 4 large sweet potatoes, 8 oz piloncillo, cinnamon, star anise, clove, 2 cups water, 50 minutes covered then 15 to 20 uncovered. Grupo Animal adds orange slices and calls it a market-stall classic.

recipes.name: Huevos a la Mexicana
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, large curds of egg scrambled with onion, tomato and serrano, the green, white and red of the flag, fresh and a little hot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs give complete protein, choline and vitamin B12, and the tomato and chile add vitamin C for very little fat.

components.note: about 1 cup refried beans, black or pinto, on the side

instructions: Chop the onion, serrano and tomato into pieces about 1 cm across.

Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion for about 1 minute, add the serrano and tomato and cook about 2 minutes more, so the vegetables soften but keep their shape.

Pour in the eggs, season with salt and leave them about 2 minutes, then fold the vegetables gently through. Cook 1 to 2 minutes more without overmixing, so the curds stay large, until the eggs are just set.
Serve at once with refried beans and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: Eggs are one of the richest food sources.

citations.source: Mexico in My Kitchen, Mexican Style Scrambled Eggs (Huevos a la Mexicana)
La Opinión, 5 formas de cocinar huevos muy a la mexicana

recipes.curationNote: Followed Mely Martínez: 4 eggs, 1/3 cup onion, 1 serrano, 2 plum tomatoes, 1 tablespoon oil, beans and tortillas on the side. La Opinión gives the same order: onion, chile and tomato fried first, the eggs left a minute, then stirred and cooked 2 to 3 minutes more.

recipes.name: Huevos Motuleños
recipes.flavorProfile: Fried tortillas spread with black beans, topped with fried eggs and habanero tomato sauce, then showered with ham, peas, fresh cheese and sweet fried plantain.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs, beans and ham give plenty of protein and the black beans add fibre and iron, though the frying and ham make this a hearty breakfast for an active morning.

components.note: about 1 cup black bean refritos, strained smooth

instructions: Boil the peas in water for 4 to 6 minutes until tender and drain. Have the chiltomate hot and the beans warm and smooth.
Heat the lard in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the plantain slices 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden and drain them.
In the same fat, pass the tortillas through for a few seconds a side so they soften without browning. Drain them.
Fry the eggs in the remaining fat, 2 to 3 minutes, keeping the yolks soft.
On each plate lay a tortilla, spread it with beans, add a second tortilla and a fried egg, or two eggs side by side. Cover with the hot chiltomate.
Finish with the ham, peas and cheese, and lay the fried plantain beside the eggs. Serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, beans and ham.
From the black beans and peas.

citations.source: Excélsior, Huevos motuleños: el clásico yucateco para desayunar en casa
El Universal, Cómo se hacen los huevos motuleños (Maricruz Avalos)

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior gives 4 eggs, 4 tortillas, 1 cup black beans, a tomato and habanero sauce, ½ cup ham, ½ cup peas, ½ cup queso fresco and fried plantain. El Universal confirms strained black beans, chiltomate and tortillas fried without browning. Both sauce and beans come from the listed bases.

recipes.name: Huevos Rancheros
recipes.flavorProfile: Lightly crisp fried corn tortillas under fried eggs with runny yolks, covered in warm tomato and chile ranchera sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs give complete protein and the tomato sauce adds vitamin C and lycopene, while the fried tortillas add energy, so beans on the side round it out.

components.note: about 1 cup refried beans on the side

instructions: Warm the salsa ranchera in a small pan and keep it hot.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Fry the tortillas one at a time for about 30 seconds a side, until lightly crisp but still bendable. Drain on paper towels.
In the same pan, fry the eggs 2 to 3 minutes, keeping the yolks whole and soft, and season with a pinch of salt.
Lay two tortillas side by side on each plate, spoon a little salsa over them, set the eggs on top and finish with more salsa. Serve with refried beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beans and corn tortillas.

citations.source: Maricruz Avalos, Huevos Rancheros Mexicanos
La Opinión, 5 formas de cocinar huevos muy a la mexicana

recipes.curationNote: Followed Maricruz Avalos for 2: 4 eggs, 4 corn tortillas fried until lightly crisp, eggs fried in the same pan, salsa under and over, refried beans on the side. La Opinión confirms tortilla passed through oil, eggs on top and bathed in ranchera sauce. The sauce is the listed salsa ranchera base.

recipes.name: Papadzules
recipes.flavorProfile: Tortillas dipped in a pale green sauce of ground pumpkin seed and epazote, rolled around chopped hard-boiled egg and topped with tomato habanero sauce and drops of green pepita oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pumpkin seeds bring magnesium, zinc, iron and good fats, and the eggs add protein, so this Maya dish is nourishing with no meat at all.

ingredients.cutPrep: hulled, lightly toasted and finely ground
a bunch of leaves and tender stems

instructions: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel and chop them.
Bring the water to a boil with the epazote and salt and simmer 5 to 8 minutes. Strain and keep the broth warm.
Toast the pumpkin seeds lightly in a dry pan over low heat, stirring, until they start to pop, without browning them. Grind them very finely.
Knead the ground seed with a few spoons of the warm epazote broth until a little green oil comes out; collect it in a cup and keep it for the top.
Blend or whisk the seed paste with enough warm epazote broth to make a light cream. Keep it warm in a bowl set over hot water, never over direct heat, or it splits.

Dip each warm tortilla in the pumpkin seed sauce, fill with chopped egg and roll it up. Lay three on each plate, cover with more seed sauce, spoon the chiltomate on top and finish with drops of the green oil.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pumpkin seeds are one of the richest sources.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta de papadzules, sabor maya para el desayuno
Por Esto, La receta original para preparar papadzules yucatecos
UTSA La Cocina Histórica, Papadzules 2000 (CONACULTA)

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior: 250 g pepita, a bunch of epazote boiled 5 to 8 minutes in 1 litre water, 12 tortillas, 6 eggs boiled 10 minutes. Por Esto warns that the sauce splits over direct heat and is kept warm in a water bath. The CONACULTA recipe gives the kneading for the green oil.

recipes.name: Caldo de Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, golden chicken broth full of chicken pieces, carrot, potato, chayote and squash with a little rice, brightened with lime, onion and serrano at the table.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, warming soup with protein from the chicken and vitamins and potassium from the vegetables, and the stock gives fluids and some minerals when someone is unwell.
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a large pot with the tomato halves. Add the chicken, lower to a simmer and skim off the foam that rises in the first 10 minutes.
Add the carrot and rice and simmer 10 minutes, then add the potato and chayote and simmer about 15 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through and the potato is nearly tender.
Add the squash and the cilantro sprigs, simmer 3 to 5 minutes until the squash is just tender, then turn off the heat and leave it covered for 4 minutes. Taste and add salt.
Serve each bowl with a piece of chicken and some of every vegetable, with chopped onion, serrano, lime and hot tortillas at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potato, chayote and squash.

citations.source: Cookpad México, Caldo de Pollo con verduras (Cynthia Serena)
Grupo Animal, 10 recetas de caldos y sopas mexicanas para apapachar el frío

recipes.curationNote: The soup is built on the listed chicken stock base, with drumsticks and thighs cooked in it. Cynthia Serena: legs and thighs, tomato, potatoes, carrots, squash added last, ½ cup rice, lime and chopped onion at the table. Grupo Animal adds chayote and cuts the vegetables in even cubes, carrot first. The bouillon cube was left out.

recipes.name: Caldo de Res
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, beefy broth from slow-simmered shank on the bone, with big pieces of corn on the cob, carrot, chayote, potato and squash, finished with lime and serrano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef shank gives protein, iron and zinc, and the long simmer draws collagen into the broth, while the vegetables add fibre and potassium.
instructions: Put the water in a large pot with the garlic, the half onion, the cilantro and the celery. Add the washed beef and the salt, cover and simmer over low heat, skimming the foam, for 2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and comes away from the bone and tendon.

Lift out the meat and strain the broth, throwing away the spent onion, cilantro, celery and garlic. Return the broth and meat to the pot. For a leaner broth, chill it overnight and lift off the solid fat.

Bring the broth back to a simmer. Add the corn, carrot and whole serranos and cook 10 minutes, then the potato and chayote for 10 to 12 minutes, and last the squash and cabbage for 5 minutes, so every vegetable is just tender.
Take out the serranos if you want less heat. Serve the beef and vegetables in deep bowls with plenty of broth, and lime, chopped onion and hot tortillas at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potato, chayote and corn.

citations.source: Telediario, Ideal para el frío: receta tradicional de caldo de res
Grupo Animal, Receta de caldo de res reconfortante

recipes.curationNote: Both sources: 1 kg chambarete, 2 ears of corn, 2 carrots, 2 chayotes, 1 large potato, a bunch of cilantro, onion, 2 serranos, 1 garlic clove, simmered slowly until the meat falls from the bone, strained, then the vegetables cooked separately to just tender. Telediario adds celery; Grupo Animal suggests squash and cabbage. The powdered bouillon both use was left out and the salt kept moderate.

recipes.name: Menudo Rojo (Pancita)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, gelatinous red chile broth full of tender beef tripe and cow foot, earthy with guajillo and ancho, finished at the table with onion, oregano, chile and lime.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tripe and cow foot are lean protein and rich in collagen, and the dried chiles add vitamin A, though the broth is rich and best eaten in a moderate bowl.

ingredients.name: beef tripe (honeycomb, book and smooth, mixed)
ingredients.cutPrep: cleaned and cut in bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: cow foot
ingredients.cutPrep: cleaned and cut in four by the butcher
toasted and crumbled, for the table

instructions: Rub the tripe and cow foot well with coarse salt and lime juice under cold running water. Rinse, then soak them in fresh water with the vinegar for 20 minutes and rinse again.

Put the meat in a large pot with the water, the halved garlic head, the whole onion and the bay leaves. Simmer over medium heat for about 2 hours 30 minutes, skimming off the foam, until the tripe is tender. A pressure cooker takes about 50 minutes from when it reaches pressure.

Meanwhile, toast the dried chiles lightly on a dry comal for a few seconds a side and soak them in hot water for 15 minutes. Blend them with the roasted tomato, garlic cloves, quarter onion, cumin, pepper, oregano, clove and a cup of the cooking broth until very smooth, then strain.

Heat the lard in a pan and fry the chile purée 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens. Pour it into the pot, take the cow foot off the bone and return the meat, add the epazote and simmer about 40 minutes more so the flavours meet. Taste for salt.
Serve very hot, with chopped onion, oregano, crumbled chile de árbol, lime halves and hot tortillas at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tripe and cow foot.
From the cow foot and tripe, which gives the broth body.

citations.source: Excélsior, Cómo hacer pancita tradicional: la receta de los domingos
Grupo Animal, Cómo preparar menudo de res rojo

recipes.curationNote: Quantities and method from Excélsior: 1.5 kg mixed tripe, 1 cow foot, salt and lime scrub, ½ cup vinegar soak, 2 hours 30 minutes, then a strained adobo of guajillo, ancho, pasilla, tomato, garlic, onion, cumin, pepper, oregano and clove fried in lard. Grupo Animal confirms skimming the broth and simmering about 40 minutes after the chile goes in. Pozole corn, added in parts of the north, was left out.

recipes.name: Pozole Rojo
recipes.flavorProfile: Big, bloomed kernels of hominy and tender pork in a brick red broth of guajillo and ancho, piled at the table with crisp lettuce, radish, onion, oregano and lime.
recipes.healthBenefit: Nixtamalized hominy gives fibre and niacin, the pork protein and zinc, and the fresh garnishes add crunch and vitamin C to a filling party dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: toasted and ground, for the table

instructions: Put the pork in a large pot with the water, half the onion, the whole garlic head, the bay leaves, cumin and salt. Simmer about 1 hour 30 minutes, skimming the foam, until the meat is tender. Lift out the meat, cut or shred it and strain the broth.
Meanwhile, toast the chiles lightly on a dry comal for a few seconds without burning them and soak them in hot water for 10 to 15 minutes, until soft.

Blend the chiles with the 2 garlic cloves, the piece of onion, the oregano and a cup of the broth until very smooth, and strain to remove the skins. Fry the purée in the oil for about 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the hominy and the chile purée to the hot broth and simmer 30 to 40 minutes over low heat, until the kernels bloom open. Return the meat and heat through, then taste for salt.
Serve in deep bowls, with lettuce, radish, onion, oregano, lime, ground chile de árbol and tostadas at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: Nixtamalization frees the niacin in the corn.

citations.source: Azteca Jalisco, Pozole rojo de Jalisco: así se prepara el tradicional platillo de las fiestas patrias
El Universal, Receta de salsa para pozole rojo

recipes.curationNote: Azteca Jalisco: 2 kg precooked pozolero corn, 1.5 kg pork, guajillo and ancho, a head of garlic, onion, 3 bay leaves, oregano and cumin, the strained chile sauce added with the corn and simmered 30 to 40 minutes. The chile sauce follows El Universal: 5 guajillo, 3 ancho softened, blended with garlic, onion and oregano and fried 5 minutes. Five guajillo and four ancho sit between the two sources.

recipes.name: Pozole Verde
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender pork and bloomed hominy in a green broth thickened with toasted pumpkin seeds, tart with tomatillo and fragrant with epazote, cilantro and radish leaves.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pumpkin seeds bring magnesium, zinc and healthy fats, the hominy fibre and niacin, and the green sauce a load of leafy herbs and vitamin C.
instructions: Put the pork in a large pot with the water, the halved onion, the garlic head, bay leaves, thyme and salt. Simmer 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, skimming the foam, until tender. Lift out the meat, shred or cut it, and strain the broth.
Add the hominy to the broth and keep it at a gentle simmer while the sauce is made.

Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, for 4 to 6 minutes, until they puff and start to pop; do not let them brown. Simmer the tomatillos, poblanos and serranos in water for 8 to 10 minutes, until the tomatillos turn olive green.
Blend the seeds, tomatillos, chiles, garlic, the piece of onion, cilantro, epazote, radish leaves, cumin and oregano with about 2 cups of the broth until smooth.

Heat the oil in a pan and fry the green sauce for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until it darkens a shade and thickens. Stir it into the pot with the meat, season with salt and simmer 5 to 10 minutes more without boiling hard, which can split the seed sauce.
Serve in deep bowls with lettuce, radish, onion, oregano, lime, chile piquín and tostadas at the table.

citations.source: Mexico In My Kitchen, Mexican Green Pozole Soup (Guerrero Style)
Uno TV, Pozole verde: la receta más sencilla

recipes.curationNote: Mexico In My Kitchen (serves 10): 6 lb pork leg and ribs, 2 cups pumpkin seeds, 2 poblanos, 2 to 3 serranos, 1 lb tomatillo, cilantro, epazote, radish leaves, cumin and oregano, fried about 7 minutes and simmered 5. Uno TV (serves 6 to 8): 1 kg pork, 200 g tomatillos, a quarter cup of seeds, poblano or jalapeño. Amounts sit between the two for 8 bowls. Written with its sauce inline rather than the pipián base, since both sources build the pozole sauce from the broth itself.

recipes.name: Pozole Blanco
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, clean pork and corn broth with soft, flowered hominy, left plain so each bowl is seasoned at the table with chile, oregano, lime, radish and lettuce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Hominy gives fibre and niacin, the pork protein and zinc, and the long simmer of meat on the bone makes a broth rich in gelatin.

ingredients.name: pork head or spine (espinazo)
ingredients.cutPrep: cut in pieces by the butcher

instructions: Put the meat in a large pot with the water, one onion, 3 garlic cloves, the bay leaves, allspice and salt. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until the meat comes away from the bone.
In a second pot, cover the hominy with water, add the remaining half onion and 2 garlic cloves and simmer 40 minutes to 1 hour, until the kernels open like flowers. Drain.
Lift the meat from the broth, take out the bones and cut or shred it. Strain the broth over the hominy, add the meat back and simmer 10 to 15 minutes together. Taste for salt.
Serve plain and white in deep bowls, with lettuce, radish, onion, oregano, lime, chile piquín and tostadas for each person to add.

nutritionHighlights.note: Nixtamalized corn makes its niacin available.

citations.source: Milenio, Pozole blanco: receta fácil e ingredientes
Uno TV, Cuánto cuesta preparar pozole blanco para 10 personas (receta de Profeco)

recipes.curationNote: Milenio: 1 kg precooked corn and 1.5 kg pork (head, spine and maciza), one and a half onions, 4 to 5 garlic cloves, the corn cooked apart until it flowers, the meat 1.5 to 2 hours. Uno TV citing Profeco (serves 10): 1 kg corn, 2 kg pork head and spine, 2 bay leaves, 4 allspice berries, romaine, radish, lime, oregano and piquín. The meat amount follows Milenio.

recipes.name: Sopa de Lima
recipes.flavorProfile: Light chicken broth scented with the bitter, floral peel of Yucatecan lima, with shredded chicken, sweet pepper and tomato, finished with crisp fried tortilla strips.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, warming soup with lean chicken protein and vitamin C from the tomato, pepper and citrus; most of the fat sits in the tortilla strips.

components.note: about 2 cups of shredded chicken breast
6 tortillas cut in strips and fried

ingredients.cutPrep: in place of 1 and a half chile dulce, chopped

ingredients.name: lima agria (Yucatecan sweet lime)
ingredients.prepNote: substitute 3 parts lime juice to 1 part orange juice

instructions: Cut the tortillas in thin strips and fry them in hot oil in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper and salt lightly.
Melt the lard in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion, garlic and pepper for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft. Add the tomato and cook 5 to 7 minutes more, until it breaks down.
Pour in the broth, add the oregano, pepper and clove and simmer 10 minutes. Add the shredded chicken and the lima juice and taste for salt.
Add the lima slices only in the last 2 to 3 minutes, since the peel turns the broth bitter if it simmers longer. Serve at once with the tortilla strips and cilantro on top.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomato, pepper and lima.

citations.source: Excélsior, Auténtica sopa de lima yucateca lista en menos de 30 minutos
Grupo Animal, Cómo hacer sopa de lima tradicional

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior: 1 shredded chicken breast, 1 onion, 4 tomatoes, 4 garlic cloves, 1 and a half chile dulce, 1.5 L stock, 3 limas, oregano and pepper, 2 cups fried tortilla strips; bell pepper and the 3 to 1 lime and orange mix are its stated substitutes. Grupo Animal fries in lard and adds cumin, clove and oregano, and adds the lima slices a few minutes before serving. Lard follows Grupo Animal; the chicken broth and shredded chicken come from the bases.

recipes.name: Agua de Horchata
recipes.flavorProfile: Cold, milky and sweet rice drink with cinnamon and vanilla, smooth and creamy in the paletería style.
recipes.healthBenefit: A treat drink: most of its energy comes from the rice and the sweetened condensed milk, with some calcium from the evaporated milk.

ingredients.cutPrep: boiled, then cooled with the rice

instructions: Bring the water to a boil for a couple of minutes, take it off the heat and add the rice and canela. Leave to cool, then refrigerate overnight, 8 to 12 hours.
Blend the rice with the canela and the soaking water until fine, 1 to 2 minutes, and strain through a fine sieve or cloth.
Return the rice water to the blender with the condensed milk, evaporated milk and vanilla and blend a few seconds until creamy.
Chill, stir well before pouring since the starch settles, and serve over plenty of ice. For a lighter horchata, skip both milks, sweeten with sugar and dilute half and half with water.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the rice and condensed milk.
From the evaporated and condensed milk.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta de agua de horchata al estilo de La Michoacana
Uno TV, Receta de agua de horchata estilo paletería
Cookpad México, Horchata de arroz

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior and Uno TV agree: 1 cup rice and a canela stick soaked overnight in 1 L water brought to a boil, blended, strained, then blended with a can each of condensed and evaporated milk and vanilla. The lighter version in the last step follows Cookpad (rice soaked with sugar and canela, diluted half with water at the glass). Seven glasses of about 250 ml.

recipes.name: Agua de Jamaica
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep ruby, tart and cranberry-like hibiscus water, sweetened just enough and served very cold.
recipes.healthBenefit: Hibiscus brings anthocyanins and a sharp tartness; nearly all the energy is from the added sugar, so the amount can be brought down to taste.

ingredients.cutPrep: brewed from 70 g dried flor de jamaica (2 cups)
ingredients.prepNote: 500 ml for the infusion, 1.5 L cold water to dilute

instructions: Rinse the dried flowers quickly in a sieve under cold water without leaving them to soak.
Bring 500 ml of water to a boil, add the flowers (and canela, if using) and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, no longer than 15, which pulls out bitter tannins. Cover off the heat and leave 20 minutes.
Stir in the sugar while the infusion is still warm until no grains remain, then strain the concentrate into a large jug.
Add the 1.5 litres of cold water, taste for sweetness and chill. Serve over ice.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta de agua de jamaica, la tradicional de las fonditas mexicanas
Cookpad México, Agua de Jamaica

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior: 2 cups dried flowers, 2 L water split as 500 ml to infuse and 1.5 L to dilute, three quarters of a cup of sugar or grated piloncillo, simmered 8 to 10 minutes and rested 20, never over 15 minutes boiling. Cookpad: 200 g flowers boiled for 2 L, with lime and mint as an option. The flowers are entered as the brewed hibiscus infusion, since the database holds the brewed tea rather than the dried calyx.

recipes.name: Agua de Tamarindo
recipes.flavorProfile: Brown, sweet and sour tamarind water with a faint caramel note, thick with fine pulp and very refreshing over ice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tamarind pulp brings fibre, potassium and magnesium; the sugar can be cut back, since ripe pulp is already sweet.

ingredients.cutPrep: pulp from 500 g pods, shells and fibres removed
1.5 L to cook, 2 L to dilute

instructions: Press the pods to crack the shells, peel away the shell and the fibrous strings, and rinse the sticky pulp briefly under cold water.
Simmer the pulp in 1.5 litres of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until it swells and turns very soft. Off the heat, stir in the sugar until dissolved and let cool until warm.
With clean hands, rub the pulp off the seeds in the pot and discard the seeds. Blend the pulp and its liquid for 30 to 45 seconds and strain into a jug.
Add the remaining 2 litres of cold water, stir and chill. Stir again before serving, since the pulp settles, and pour over ice with a slice of lime.

nutritionHighlights.note: Some fine pulp stays in the drink.

citations.source: Excélsior, Prepara una deliciosa agua de tamarindo
Grupo Animal, Cómo hacer agua de tamarindo, fresca y deliciosa

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior: 500 g pods in their shells, 3.5 L water with 1.5 L used to cook the pulp 15 to 20 minutes, 1 to 1 and a quarter cups sugar or piloncillo, seeds rubbed off by hand, blended and strained. Grupo Animal: 500 g tamarind, 2 L water, 1 cup sugar, boiled 20 minutes and mashed. Shelled pulp weighed at about 400 g from 500 g pods. Twelve glasses of about 300 ml.

recipes.name: Agua de Sandía
recipes.flavorProfile: Pink, light and sweet watermelon water sharpened with lime, the simplest and most summery of the aguas frescas.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly water with watermelon, it hydrates and gives vitamin C and lycopene; the sugar is optional when the fruit is ripe.

ingredients.cutPrep: flesh only, seeds removed, in cubes

instructions: Cut the watermelon flesh in cubes and blend with the lime juice, the sugar and about 500 ml of the water for 1 minute, until smooth.
Strain if a finer drink is wanted, or leave the pulp in.
Pour into a jug with the rest of the cold water, taste for sweetness and chill 1 to 2 hours. Serve over ice.

citations.source: Fundación Casa de México en España, Agua de sandía y limón
Directo al Paladar, Agua de sandía

recipes.curationNote: Casa de México (8 servings): 1 kg seeded watermelon, 3 limes, 100 g sugar optional, 2 L water, blended with part of the water and strained if wanted. Directo al Paladar: 400 g watermelon, 300 ml water, 30 ml lime juice, 30 g sugar, blended 1 minute. Amounts follow Casa de México.

recipes.name: Atole de Masa
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, thick and silky corn drink sweetened with piloncillo and scented with canela and a touch of star anise, the breakfast partner of tamales.
recipes.healthBenefit: Nixtamalized corn gives slow carbohydrate, some fibre and calcium from the cal; the piloncillo adds sugar, so the amount can be eased back.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1.5 L to heat, 500 ml to dissolve the masa

ingredients.name: star anise
ingredients.cutPrep: half a star is enough for a subtle note

instructions: Put 1.5 litres of water in a pot with the piloncillo, canela and star anise and heat over medium until the piloncillo dissolves and the water starts to bubble.
Meanwhile blend or work the masa with the remaining 500 ml of water until smooth, with no lumps.

Pour the dissolved masa into the pot little by little, stirring all the time. Cook 15 to 20 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly so it does not catch, until it thickens and loses its raw corn taste.
If it gets too thick, add a little more water. Strain out the canela and anise and serve hot.

citations.source: El Universal, Cómo hacer atole de maíz y qué aporta
Cookpad México, Atole de masa con piloncillo

recipes.curationNote: El Universal: 1 L water, half a cup of piloncillo, half a canela stick, half a star anise, 500 g masa, cooked 15 minutes stirring, thinned with water if needed and strained. Cookpad (12 servings): 500 g masa, 4 L water, canela and piloncillo to taste. The water sits between the two at 2 L.

recipes.name: Atolillo (Atole de Arroz)
recipes.flavorProfile: A warm, creamy rice and milk drink, sweet and scented with canela and a little vanilla, thick enough to coat the spoon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk gives calcium and protein, and the rice an easy, gentle starch that suits a cold morning or an upset stomach.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in water 1 to 2 hours, drained

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.cutPrep: optional, dissolved in a little cold milk, for a thicker atole

instructions: Soak the rice in water for 1 to 2 hours, drain it and blend it with the 500 ml of fresh water until it is very fine.
Pour the rice water into a pot with the canela and cook over medium heat, stirring all the time, for 8 to 10 minutes, until it thickens and the rice is cooked.
Add the milk and sugar and keep cooking over low heat, stirring so it does not catch, for 15 to 20 minutes. Stir in the cornstarch now if a thicker atole is wanted and cook 3 to 5 minutes more.
Take it off the heat, stir in the vanilla, lift out the canela and serve hot in cups.

citations.source: Larousse Cocina, Atole de arroz (Margarita Carrillo)
Recetas de México, Atole de arroz

recipes.curationNote: Larousse Cocina (4 to 6): half a cup of soaked rice cooked in half a litre of water, then 1 L milk, three quarters of a cup of sugar and canela, 15 to 20 minutes. Recetas de México (4): 200 g rice blended with half the milk, 1 L milk, 120 g sugar, canela, half a teaspoon of vanilla. The cornstarch is optional and follows the thicker Guatemalan atolillo style.

recipes.name: Licuado de Plátano con Avena
recipes.flavorProfile: A cold, thick breakfast licuado of ripe banana, milk and oats, sweetened with honey and dusted with cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Banana brings potassium, oats soluble fibre (beta-glucan), and milk protein and calcium, which makes this a filling breakfast in a glass.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the banana, milk, oats, honey, vanilla and ice in the blender.
Blend on high for 1 to 2 minutes, until the oats are fully broken down and the licuado is smooth and frothy.
Pour into glasses, dust with cinnamon and drink right away, before the oats thicken it further.

citations.source: Cocina Fácil, Licuado de plátano con avena
Cookpad México, Licuado de plátano con avena

recipes.curationNote: Cocina Fácil (1): 1 ripe banana, half a cup of oats, 1 tbsp honey, 1 cup milk, ice. Cookpad (4): 2 bananas, 1 L milk, 6 tbsp oats, 3 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp vanilla, cinnamon. Scaled to 2 glasses between the two. This is the batido de plátano asked for, under the name it goes by in Mexican kitchens.

recipes.name: Café de Olla
recipes.flavorProfile: Coffee brewed in a clay pot with piloncillo, canela, clove and orange peel: dark, sweet and spiced, with a light citrus finish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Coffee carries polyphenols such as chlorogenic acid, and the cinnamon and clove add aromatic compounds; the piloncillo is still sugar, so a cup is a treat.

ingredients.name: ground coffee, dark roast, medium-coarse grind

instructions: Put the water, piloncillo, canela, cloves and orange peel in a clay pot (olla de barro) or saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring until the piloncillo dissolves, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the coffee, cover and let it steep 5 to 10 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth into cups and serve hot.

citations.source: Casa de México, Café de olla
México en mi Cocina, Cómo hacer café de olla

recipes.curationNote: México en mi Cocina (4 cups): 4 cups water, 3 oz piloncillo, half a canela stick, 4 tbsp coffee, added off the heat and rested 5 minutes. Casa de México (10): 3 L water, 500 g coffee, 250 g piloncillo, 2 oranges of zest, 3 cloves, canela, star anise optional, steeped 10 minutes on very low heat. Ground coffee is listed outside the database because its entries are brewed coffee only.

recipes.name: Champurrado
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, hot chocolate atole of corn masa, Mexican table chocolate and piloncillo, frothed with a molinillo and scented with canela.
recipes.healthBenefit: Nixtamalized masa gives calcium and niacin, cacao brings polyphenols and magnesium, and the milk adds protein; it is sweet and rich, a cold-weather drink.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 litre plus 1 cup to dissolve the masa

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Bring 1 litre of the water to a boil with the canela and piloncillo and simmer until the piloncillo dissolves, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the milk and the chocolate and stir over medium heat until the chocolate melts, 3 to 5 minutes.
Dissolve the masa in the remaining cup of water, working out every lump with your fingers, and strain it.

Pour the masa into the pot in a thin stream, beating all the while with a molinillo or whisk so it does not lump. Add the salt and keep cooking over low heat, stirring, for 10 to 15 minutes, until it thickens and loses any raw corn taste.
Lift out the canela, froth once more with the molinillo and serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the nixtamalized masa and the milk.

citations.source: Excélsior, Receta tradicional de champurrado
El Imparcial, Esta es la receta del mejor champurrado

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior: 1 L water plus a cup, 2 to 3 chocolate tablets, a small cone of piloncillo, canela, half a cup of masa poured in a thread under the molinillo. El Imparcial (6): 1 L milk, 1 L water, half a cup of masa, 2 tablets, half a cup of piloncillo, canela and a pinch of salt. Written mostly with water, the older way, with a little milk.

recipes.name: Chocolate Caliente Mexicano
recipes.flavorProfile: Milk beaten with stone-ground Mexican chocolate, canela and vanilla until a thick foam rises, slightly gritty with sugar and almond in the old style.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cacao brings magnesium, iron and flavanols, the milk calcium and protein, and the almonds vitamin E; it is sweet, so a cup is a treat.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Heat the milk with the canela over medium heat until it is steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the chocolate, the ground almonds if used and the sugar, and stir until the chocolate melts.
Beat with a molinillo, rolling it between your palms, or with a whisk, for 8 to 10 minutes on low heat, until a thick foam covers the top. Do not let it boil over.
Stir in the vanilla, lift out the canela and serve with its foam.

citations.source: El Universal, Cómo hacer chocolate caliente
Pati Jinich, Chocolate caliente mexicano

recipes.curationNote: El Universal (6): 2 L milk, canela, a vanilla pod, 2 metate chocolate tablets, half a cup of sugar, beaten 8 to 10 minutes. Pati Jinich (2): 2 cups milk or water, 120 g chocolate, a 5 cm canela stick, 1 tsp vanilla, 4 tbsp ground almonds, 4 tbsp sugar. Water in place of milk is the older Oaxacan way.

recipes.name: Licuado de Mamey
recipes.flavorProfile: A cold, thick licuado of ripe mamey, with its sweet pumpkin and almond taste, blended with milk and finished with cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mamey sapote is high in fibre, vitamin C, vitamin B6 and carotenoids, and the milk brings calcium and protein.

ingredients.name: mamey sapote
ingredients.cutPrep: 1 ripe mamey, flesh only, seed removed

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Cut the mamey in half, take out the large seed and scoop out the orange flesh.
Blend the mamey with the milk, sugar, vanilla and ice for 1 to 2 minutes, until smooth.
Pour into glasses, sprinkle with ground cinnamon and serve cold.

citations.source: México en mi Cocina, Licuado de mamey
Cocina Vital, Licuado de mamey con vainilla

recipes.curationNote: México en mi Cocina (2): 1 mamey, 2 cups cold milk, 2 cups ice, 2 tbsp sugar, cinnamon on top. Cocina Vital (2): 1 ripe mamey, 1 tsp vanilla, 500 ml milk, 2 tbsp sugar, cinnamon. Mamey sapote is not in the database; the mammy apple there is a different fruit.

recipes.name: Ponche Navideño
recipes.flavorProfile: A hot Christmas fruit punch of tejocote, guava, apple, sugarcane, tamarind and prunes, simmered with canela, jamaica and piloncillo until fragrant.
recipes.healthBenefit: Guava is very high in vitamin C, and the fruit adds fibre and potassium; it is sweetened, and the fruit pieces are eaten from the cup with a spoon.

ingredients.cutPrep: a handful of dried jamaica flowers, steeped in the pot

instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the canela, piloncillo, tamarind and jamaica, and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until the piloncillo dissolves and the water turns red. Strain out the jamaica and tamarind pods if a clear punch is wanted.
Add the tejocotes, sugarcane and apple and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the guava, prunes and raisins and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until all the fruit is soft and the punch smells of it.
Serve hot in cups with fruit pieces and a stick of sugarcane in each.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fruit eaten with the punch.

citations.source: Mama Latina Tips, Ponche mexicano navideño
UTSA La Cocina, Ponche de Navidad

recipes.curationNote: Mama Latina Tips (40 cups): 12 L water, 5 apples, 12 guavas, 20 tejocotes, 2 sugarcanes, a quarter kilo of prunes, 2 handfuls of jamaica, 5 canela sticks, 1.2 kg sugar, simmered 30 to 45 minutes. UTSA (6): 1 lb tamarind, 1 lb guava, 2 sugarcane pieces, 8 oz tejocote, canela, prunes and raisins, simmered 25 then 20 minutes. Scaled to 12 cups with piloncillo for the sweetener. The jamaica is listed as its brewed tea, since it is steeped in the pot.

recipes.name: Pozol de Cacao
recipes.flavorProfile: A cool, thin drink of nixtamalized corn masa and toasted cacao dissolved in water, earthy and lightly bitter; left to sour for a few days, it turns tart.
recipes.healthBenefit: Nixtamalized corn gives calcium and niacin, cacao magnesium and polyphenols. Soured pozol is a traditional lactic ferment studied for its lactic acid bacteria, though benefits in people are not established.

ingredients.cutPrep: cacao beans toasted, peeled and ground with the masa

instructions: Toast the cacao beans in a dry comal over medium heat, turning them, for 8 to 12 minutes, until fragrant and the shells crack. Peel them while warm.
Grind the cacao with the masa (in a molino, a metate or a food processor) into one even, dark dough and shape it into balls.
For pozol agrio, wrap the balls in banana leaves or a cloth and keep them at warm room temperature for 4 to 5 days, until they smell pleasantly sour. For fresh pozol skip this step.

To serve, break a ball into a jícara or glass and dissolve it in the water with your hand until it is a thin, watery atole. Sweeten with piloncillo, add the cinnamon and salt if wanted, and serve with ice.

citations.source: Amigos de MAP, Pozol tabasqueño
Cocina Vital, Cómo preparar pozol de cacao
Infobae, Pozol, la bebida ancestral tabasqueña

recipes.curationNote: Amigos de MAP (16 cups): 1 kg nixtamalized corn and 200 g toasted, peeled cacao ground together and thinned with 4 L boiled water. Cocina Vital (4): 250 g masa, 80 g cacao, 1 L water, 80 g piloncillo, half a teaspoon of cinnamon, salt. Infobae, quoting Tabasco agriculture officials: pozol agrio ferments 4 to 5 days, sometimes two weeks. Cacao beans are listed as cocoa mass, the database entry nearest to ground whole beans. Tier is weak because the health effects of the ferment rest on microbiology studies, not trials.
